critical_issues.msg: JWT_SECRET falls back to a hardcoded in-band value 'dev-jwt-secret' when the environment variable is absent, defeating production secret requirements
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove the fallback: jwt_secret = os.environ['JWT_SECRET_KEY'] (let it KeyError in production) or explicitly raise ValueError as done for FLASK_ENV=production

critical_issues.msg: Debug print statements (lines 66, 69, 71, 74) log raw JWT tokens and secrets, leaking sensitive material to stdout
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove all print statements in require_auth; replace with structured logging at DEBUG level that never outputs token values

critical_issues.msg: Debug print leaks decoded JWT payload including potentially sensitive claims
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove print statement; log only non-sensitive fields (e.g., user_id, tenant_id) if needed

critical_issues.msg: _seed_user helper defaults to tenant_id=1, but callers in TestTicketServiceIntegration and TestSLAServiceIntegration omit the tenant_id argument; tickets and users end up in different tenants causing cross-tenant data leaks or NotFoundException failures.
critical_issues.suggestion: Change the default to require_explicit: def _seed_user(async_session, tenant_id: int, **overrides) and update all callers to pass tenant_id explicitly, e.g. _seed_user(async_session, tenant_id) everywhere.

critical_issues.msg: _seed_customer helper also defaults to tenant_id=1; same cross-tenant data issue as _seed_user above.
critical_issues.suggestion: Change the default to require_explicit: def _seed_customer(async_session, tenant_id: int, **overrides) and update all callers to pass tenant_id explicitly.

suggestions.msg: Plan file describing the full ticket management UI implementation; no code issues present.
useCustomers(1, 100) fetches a page of customers just to look up one name by ID; if the customer is beyond page 100 the name will be missing from the sidebar link.
suggestions.suggestion: Create a useCustomer(id) query (already exported in queries.ts) and fetch by ticket.customer_id directly: const { data: customerData } = useCustomer(Number(ticket.customer_id)); const customerName = customerData?.data?.name.

suggestions.msg: initials() calls n[0] on every space-split token; if created_by is null/undefined/empty-string, n[0] is undefined and join produces 'UNDEFINEDUNDEFINED'.
suggestions.suggestion: Guard against empty parts: .map((n) => n && n[0] ? n[0] : '').join('')

suggestions.msg: No loading skeleton shown while useTicketReplies or useTicketActivity are pending — the replies section and activity log will flash empty then populate, creating a jarring layout shift.
suggestions.suggestion: Add const { isLoading: repliesLoading } = useTicketReplies(ticketId); const { isLoading: activityLoading } = useTicketActivity(ticketId); and render skeletons or a spinner inside the Replies and Activity cards when those flags are true.

suggestions.msg: onClick handler is attached to the <td> element itself; React treats synthetic events on <td> as non-interactive and the row-actions button may not receive stopPropagation reliably, risking the dropdown triggering unwanted navigation.
suggestions.suggestion: Move the onClick from <td className="... w-10" onClick={...}> to the <DropdownMenuTrigger> or wrap the <td> content in a div with pointer-events management.

suggestions.msg: No error handling displayed for the useCustomers call; if the customers API fails the sidebar link silently falls back to '#{customer_id}' without user feedback.
suggestions.suggestion: Destructure isError from useCustomers and display a small inline warning or log the error.

suggestions.msg: useEffect dependency array for the SLA toast check does not include toast; if the sonner toast function reference changes the effect won't re-run, though this is low-risk since sonner stable.
suggestions.suggestion: Add toast to the dependency array: useEffect(() => { ... }, [ticket, ticketId, toast]);

suggestions.msg: window.confirm() is a blocking browser dialog with a generic message; it bypasses the app's styling and accessibility conventions.
suggestions.suggestion: Replace with a confirm Dialog (Radix or shadcn Dialog) rendered inline with a destructive Cancel/Confirm pair.

suggestions.msg: PRIORITY_COLORS includes both 'normal' and 'medium' keys but the plan spec and Select options only expose 'urgent/high/medium/low', so 'normal' is dead code; if the API ever returns 'normal' the color will differ from 'medium' despite being the same priority level.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the 'normal' key from PRIORITY_COLORS: const PRIORITY_COLORS = { urgent: ..., high: ..., medium: ..., low: ... };

suggestions.msg: useEffect dependency array is missing toast; if sonner's toast function reference changes the SLA breach toasts may use a stale closure.
suggestions.suggestion: Add toast to the dependency array: useEffect(() => { ... }, [isLoading, breachedTicketIds, toast]);

suggestions.msg: Sort comparator uses av < bv ? -1 : av > bv ? 1 : 0 which coerces all values to booleans; for string values localeCompare would give more correct Unicode-aware ordering.
suggestions.suggestion: When sortKey is not 'response_deadline', use localeCompare: if (typeof av === 'string') return sortDir === 'asc' ? av.localeCompare(bv as string) : (bv as string).localeCompare(av);

suggestions.msg: After a successful bulkUpdate mutation the component calls onClear() but does not reset bulkUpdate state; if the mutation is retried on a subsequent apply it may show isPending from the previous attempt.
suggestions.suggestion: Reset mutation state after success by calling bulkUpdate.reset() in the onSuccess path before toast.success.

suggestions.msg: The assignee Select has no way to unassign tickets in bulk — the 'Assign to...' placeholder implies only 'select an agent to assign', leaving no UI affordance to clear an existing assignment.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a SelectItem value="" underneath the user options with label 'Unassign' or '—' so users can bulk-clear assignments.

suggestions.msg: Ticket card div with onClick is not keyboard-accessible (no role, tabIndex, or onKeyDown handler).
suggestions.suggestion: Add role="button" tabIndex={0} onKeyDown={(e) => e.key === 'Enter' && onClick(ticket.id)} to the div.

suggestions.msg: handleTicketClick is defined inside the component body, causing a new function reference on every render.
suggestions.suggestion: Define handleTicketClick with useCallback, or move the router.push inline into onClick.

suggestions.msg: router.push uses a hardcoded path without trailing-slash consistency — if the app normalizes URLs elsewhere, this could cause a redirect loop or mismatch.
suggestions.suggestion: Ensure all ticket navigation uses consistent URL formatting (e.g., always with or without trailing slash).

suggestions.msg: Assignee column title is 'Agent ${aid}' — exposing raw numeric ID is a poor UX and leaks internal representation.
suggestions.suggestion: Resolve agent name from a users lookup or pass agent_name in KanbanTicketData.

suggestions.msg: PRIORITY_COLORS marks 'urgent' and 'high' identically, making them visually indistinguishable in the legend.
suggestions.suggestion: Use distinct colors for 'urgent' (e.g., bg-red-600) and 'high' (bg-orange-500) to improve visual differentiation.

suggestions.msg: setInterval runs every 60 seconds but Date.now() is captured only once at render — the display only updates on re-render, so the 60s tick is wasted if the component doesn't re-render for another reason.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the unused tick state entirely and use setInterval with direct DOM update, or use useEffect to track current time in state and derive remaining from it.

suggestions.msg: Color variable is assigned via if/else ladder then conditionally overridden — colorClass can be set to one value in the if (line 58) and then replaced in the breached block (line 73). This works but is confusing.
suggestions.suggestion: Simplify color logic: compute colorClass based on breached and ratio only, removing the separate reassignment in the return statement.

suggestions.msg: Template literal `${colorClass} animate-pulse border-red-500` duplicates 'border-red-300' set inside colorClass for breached state — the border class is applied twice inconsistently.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the border-red-300 from colorClass and only use border-red-500 via the template literal when breached.

suggestions.msg: setInterval has no cleanup guarantee if the component unmounts before the effect — useEffect cleanup is present but the interval closure captures stale tick reference if the component re-renders.
suggestions.suggestion: Use a ref or state to track actual elapsed time rather than incrementing a counter.

suggestions.msg: useCustomers is called with page=undefined and pageSize=20, but the query param construction (page=${undefined}) would produce invalid URL params since undefined coerces to the string 'undefined'.
suggestions.suggestion: Use a default page value: useCustomers(page ?? 1, 20) or pass a definite page number from the parent.

suggestions.msg: initialData is typed as Partial<TicketFormData> & { id?: number }, but fields like customer_id, channel, priority, sla_level are always strings in TicketFormData — no runtime validation ensures type correctness when editing pre-existing data.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a type guard or parse initialData fields explicitly to assert their types before use.

suggestions.msg: Number(data.customer_id) is called without checking whether customer_id is 0 — a value of 0 passes Number() without NaN, potentially sending { customer_id: 0 } to the API.
suggestions.suggestion: Validate customer_id before Number(): if isNaN(Number(data.customer_id)) or data.customer_id === 0, show the form error instead of submitting.

suggestions.msg: Customers data is cast with 'as Array<{ id: number; name: string }>' — any mismatch between the actual API response shape and this type assertion will cause silent runtime errors.
suggestions.suggestion: Define a Customer type and use it for the response envelope instead of a generic cast.

suggestions.msg: useEffect that resets form on initialData change has no cleanup (no return), and since it depends on reset, eslint-plugin-react-hooks would warn about missing reset from deps if not suppressed.
suggestions.suggestion: Add reset to the dependency array: useEffect(() => { ... }, [initialData, reset]) — though this may cause infinite loops if reset is unstable.

suggestions.msg: useReminders does not type its return value with ApiEnvelope — unlike every other query hook, it omits the generic and returns an untyped response, losing compile-time safety.
suggestions.suggestion: Add <ApiEnvelope<Record<string, unknown>>> generic to the apiClient.get call in useReminders, consistent with all other hooks.

suggestions.msg: useCustomers has a parameter named pageSize but is called from ticket-form-dialog.tsx with undefined as the first argument — the function defaults pageSize to 20 but page has no such default, so the first arg becomes page.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a default: page = 1 to useCustomers signature so passing only pageSize works correctly.

suggestions.msg: PaginatedResponse and ApiEnvelope are defined locally and not exported — other parts of the codebase like ticket-form-dialog cast to local anonymous types, preventing shared use.
suggestions.suggestion: Export PaginatedResponse<T> and ApiEnvelope<T> so they can be reused across the app instead of duplicating inline Record<string, unknown> casts.

suggestions.msg: useAddReply onSuccess invalidates both ticketReplies and ticketActivity query keys, but useUpdateTicket (line 209) only invalidates the generic ['tickets'] key rather than using qk.tickets() for consistency.
suggestions.suggestion: Use qk.tickets() in useUpdateTicket onSuccess to keep query key construction centralized and consistent.

suggestions.msg: psycopg2-binary and pymysql are listed as dependencies but the project uses asyncpg for async database access; they appear unused
suggestions.suggestion: Remove psycopg2-binary and pymysql, or confirm they are consumed elsewhere in the codebase

suggestions.msg: reportlab is listed as a dependency but is not used in the reviewed files
suggestions.suggestion: Remove reportlab if it is not consumed by any reviewed file, or document where it is used

suggestions.msg: mypy is listed in dev dependencies but CLAUDE.md notes that mypy is run via pre-push hook; ruff's select does not include type-checking rules (B, TRY)
suggestions.suggestion: Ensure mypy is included in CI and that ruff ignores don't suppress type-checking gaps that mypy should catch

suggestions.msg: HTTPException is imported but only used for the two manual validation handlers at lines 158 and 162; the project pattern routes AppException subclasses to a global handler, making manual HTTPException redundant
suggestions.suggestion: Remove HTTPException import and raise a ValidationException instead, or drop the manual try/except blocks and rely on the global handler

suggestions.msg: tenant_id=ctx.tenant_id or 0 uses a fallback of 0 for None, masking whether the real tenant is 0 or simply absent from the token
suggestions.suggestion: Make tenant_id resolution explicit: raise HTTPException 401 if ctx.tenant_id is None, rather than silently coercing to 0

suggestions.msg: assignee_id filter accepts 0 via ge=0 to represent 'unassigned', but TicketBulkUpdate also accepts ge=1 for its assigned_to, creating inconsistent semantics
suggestions.suggestion: Standardise: use ge=0 consistently and treat 0 as 'no change / unassigned'; document the semantics

suggestions.msg: Manual try/except ValueError handling for status and priority enums duplicates the Pydantic model validation already done via pattern in TicketCreate/TicketUpdate
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the try/except blocks; if query params are invalid the enum constructor will raise ValueError caught by the global AppException handler

suggestions.msg: bulk_update_tickets loops over ticket_ids sequentially without transaction safety; if one update fails mid-loop the already-updated tickets stay changed (partial failure)
suggestions.suggestion: Wrap the loop in a transaction or clarify the docstring that the operation is best-effort and partial updates are intentional

suggestions.msg: bulk_update_tickets docstring promises to skip tickets from other tenants, but the code does not check whether tickets were skipped — a silently ignored class of failures
suggestions.suggestion: Collect and return the IDs of tickets that were skipped or not found, so callers can detect partial outcomes

suggestions.msg: get_sla_breach_tickets constructs SLAService with ticket_service=TicketService(session), causing two service instances and two DB sessions for what is logically one operation
suggestions.suggestion: Pass the already-instantiated TicketService from the router scope, or inject the session into SLAService and let it instantiate TicketService internally with the same session

suggestions.msg: Rule 121 violation: ticket_service is a service instance passed as an optional constructor argument, not an AsyncSession; the convention requires the single constructor arg to be session
suggestions.suggestion: Pass session: AsyncSession as the only constructor arg; instantiate TicketService(session) internally when needed, or accept it as an optional AsyncSession from the router

suggestions.msg: remaining is a timedelta; the comparison remaining.total_seconds() < warning_threshold * 3600 is redundant since remaining is already derived from response_deadline - UTC.now()
suggestions.suggestion: Simplify to remaining < timedelta(hours=warning_threshold) for clarity and correctness

suggestions.msg: calculate_remaining_time is called at line 34 but returns a timedelta; however, calculate_remaining_time on line 57 can return a raw relativedelta if response_deadline is timezone-aware and datetime.now(UTC) is subtracted — check type consistency
suggestions.suggestion: Ensure calculate_remaining_time always returns timedelta: cast result to timedelta() to guarantee type consistency across all code paths

suggestions.msg: get_breach_tickets has an awkward optional tickets parameter that is also set internally from _ticket_service; the parameter name shadows the built-in
suggestions.suggestion: Rename parameter from 'tickets' to 'ticket_list' or similar to avoid shadowing the built-in

suggestions.msg: remaining is assigned from a conditional expression but can be either a timedelta or timedelta(0) — the guard at line 37 checks total_seconds() which is correct but the logic is duplicated in check_sla_breach
suggestions.suggestion: Reuse check_sla_breach() as the single source of truth for breach detection rather than checking remaining.total_seconds() separately

suggestions.msg: _AGENT_POOL = (1, 2, 3) is a module-level constant with magic numbers; agents must be real user IDs but there is no validation that these IDs exist
suggestions.suggestion: Define _AGENT_POOL with a comment referencing the lookup source, and consider validating pool members against the users table on service init or first use

suggestions.msg: add_reply has a TOCTOU race: two concurrent replies can both pass the not ticket.first_response_at check and each set first_response_at, leaving only the last writer's timestamp
suggestions.suggestion: Use SELECT FOR UPDATE on the ticket row within the existing transaction to lock the ticket during first_response_at update, or rely on an atomic UPDATE with a WHERE clause that filters on first_response_at IS NULL

suggestions.msg: get_ticket_activity uses content.like('%ticket#{ticket_id}%') — a leading-wildcard LIKE cannot use a B-tree index and will do a full table scan on the activity table
suggestions.suggestion: Add a ticket_id column to the ActivityModel and index it, then replace the LIKE filter with a direct equality filter; alternatively add a GIN index on content if full-text search is needed

suggestions.msg: add_reply returns TicketReplyModel but does not call session.flush() before the ticket update at line 249 — the reply has been added to the session but not yet flushed, making the relative ordering of reply insert and ticket update non-deterministic at the DB level
suggestions.suggestion: Move session.add(reply) after the first_response_at update, or call await self.session.flush() before the UPDATE to ensure consistent ordering

suggestions.msg: _to_str is a module-level helper that handles both enum and string inputs; it works but the pattern is duplicated across services — consider a shared utility in pkg.utils
suggestions.suggestion: Extract _to_str to pkg.utils and import it, or rely on .value directly since the service only ever receives enum arguments from the router

suggestions.msg: Test parameterized over async_session fixture but RBACService.has_permission is a @staticmethod requiring no DB; the fixture is unused and clutters test scope.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the async_session fixture parameter from all TestRBACServiceIntegration async tests — they test static in-memory logic that doesn't need DB access. Alternatively, test only the async DB-backed methods if they are added.

suggestions.msg: Manually constructing a Ticket dataclass from models.ticket to simulate an expired ticket bypasses the ORM; the test exercises the SLA service but with a test double rather than a real persisted ticket.
suggestions.suggestion: Consider inserting a real TicketModel row directly in the DB with a past response_deadline via raw SQL, so the test exercises the full stack including SLA query logic against a real ticket record.

suggestions.msg: Same Ticket dataclass construction pattern as line 350 — test double instead of a real DB row.
suggestions.suggestion: Insert a real ticket row into the DB with a past resolved_at to test the resolved-ticket path.

suggestions.msg: Same Ticket dataclass construction pattern as line 350 — test double instead of a real DB row.
suggestions.suggestion: Insert a real ticket row into the DB with resolved_at = now() to test the resolved branch.

suggestions.msg: TriggerService.check_triggers uses page_size=10000 with no pagination boundary guard; a large campaign table could cause memory issues.
suggestions.suggestion: Use a reasonable page_size (e.g. 1000) or paginate through results.

suggestions.msg: TicketChannel, TicketPriority, TicketStatus imported from services.ticket_service rather than models.ticket where they are defined; violates project convention that enums live in models/ and services re-export them.
suggestions.suggestion: Change to: from models.ticket import TicketChannel, TicketPriority, TicketStatus

suggestions.msg: _seed_tenant returns a raw dict (result['id']), inconsistent with _seed_user/_seed_customer which return ORM object .id directly.
suggestions.suggestion: Return result.id or result['id'] consistently across all seed helpers; prefer returning ORM objects for type safety.

suggestions.msg: test_change_password calls change_password with no assertions on the result; the comment 'returns None on success' means the test passes vacuously without verifying the new password actually works.
suggestions.suggestion: Add an assertion or call auth_svc.authenticate_user(old_password) to confirm the old password fails and/or a successful auth with the new password succeeds.

suggestions.msg: _seed_customer uses hardcoded 'Test Customer' name and only f'test-{uuid}@example.com' for email variation; concurrent test runs with the same uuid segment could produce email uniqueness violations if the DB enforces unique email.
suggestions.suggestion: Include the full uuid hex in the name as well: name=f'Test Customer {uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}' to avoid name uniqueness issues if that constraint is added later.

suggestions.msg: test_assign_ticket expects ticket.assigned_to to be non-None after creation (auto-assigned), but if the agent pool (_AGENT_POOL = (1, 2, 3)) has no valid agents for this tenant, the assertion will fail in a real DB environment.
suggestions.suggestion: Seed an agent user for the tenant before creating the ticket, or mock _next_agent in integration tests, so the assertion is deterministic rather than relying on hardcoded agent IDs.

suggestions.msg: The auto-assign round-robin test does not verify round-robin ordering — only that both tickets get an integer; the test passes even if both receive the same agent.
suggestions.suggestion: Assert ticket1.assigned_to != ticket2.assigned_to (or verify expected rotation pattern) to actually test round-robin behavior.

suggestions.msg: Rule 124 violation: the mock_session fixture includes session.refresh = AsyncMock(); unit tests that call get_ticket_replies or get_ticket_activity (which call session.refresh internally) are testing with a no-op mock rather than verifying refresh behavior — could silently hide bugs where refresh fails.
suggestions.suggestion: Ensure mock_session.refresh is configured to return/populate the actual mock object passed to it, or document that refresh is intentionally a no-op in this test file.

suggestions.msg: Test name test_returns_replies_ordered_by_created_at_asc is 51 characters — exceeds the project's readable test-name guidance; consider renaming to test_replies_ordered_asc or test_replies_order_asc.
suggestions.suggestion: Shorten test name to under 45 characters: test_replies_ordered_asc.

suggestions.msg: test_breached_when_deadline_passed_and_not_resolved is a sync method but the class it lives in (TestSLABreachDetection) is not marked async — it runs fine but mixed async/sync test classes can cause pytest-asyncio discovery issues in some configurations.
suggestions.suggestion: Mark the class as @pytest.mark.unit if not already configured, and consider grouping sync SLA tests in a separate class from async reply/activity tests.

suggestions.msg: MagicMock instances lack type hints — reduces value of static analysis for test code.
suggestions.suggestion: Annotate mock_service, mock_sla_service, mock_user_service with their actual types, e.g. `mock_service: MagicMock = MagicMock()` or use `create_autospec(TicketService)` for stricter mock shapes.

suggestions.msg: Test name claims 'assignee_id_zero_rejected' but router schema enforces ge=1 (not ge=0), so this test exercises a code path that cannot exist in production.
suggestions.suggestion: Change the test to assert on a different invalid value that is actually caught by the router, e.g. assignee_id=-1, or update the router schema to also reject 0 and write a test for that scenario.

suggestions.msg: assign_ticket router calls UserService(session) to validate the assignee exists before assigning, but client_with_service only patches TicketService — the UserService call is not verified in any test.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a test that verifies UserService.get_user_by_id is called (or that a NotFoundException from UserService propagates correctly) when assigning to a non-existent user.

suggestions.msg: No test covers the assign_ticket endpoint with a non-existent assignee user — the UserService validation branch is exercised but not asserted.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a test case: mock UserService.get_user_by_id to raise NotFoundException, call PUT /api/v1/tickets/1/assign with json={"assignee_id": 99}, and assert status 404.

suggestions.msg: No tests exist for the POST /api/v1/tickets/bulk-update endpoint — the router has branching logic (assigned_to + status) that is entirely untested.
suggestions.suggestion: Add TestBulkUpdateEndpoint with cases: success with status change, success with assignment, partial-not-found (one ticket missing, others updated).

suggestions.msg: assert resp.status_code == 200 in test_success but does not verify the response body (assigned_to=5) is correctly serialized — only the mock was checked.
suggestions.suggestion: Add assertion: assert resp.json()["data"]["assigned_to"] == 5 to verify the response envelope reflects the updated ticket.

suggestions.msg: test_success for update_ticket asserts subject but not priority, channel, or assigned_to even though TicketUpdate schema accepts all three.
suggestions.suggestion: Add assertions for all fields returned in the envelope, e.g. assert body["data"]["priority"] == "medium".

warnings.suggestion: Ensure all ticket navigation uses consistent URL formatting (e.g., always with or without trailing slash).

warnings.msg: Assignee column title is 'Agent ${aid}' — exposing raw numeric ID is a poor UX and leaks internal representation.
warnings.suggestion: Resolve agent name from a users lookup or pass agent_name in KanbanTicketData.

warnings.msg: PRIORITY_COLORS marks 'urgent' and 'high' identically, making them visually indistinguishable in the legend.
warnings.suggestion: Use distinct colors for 'urgent' (e.g., bg-red-600) and 'high' (bg-orange-500) to improve visual differentiation.

warnings.msg: setInterval runs every 60 seconds but Date.now() is captured only once at render — the display only updates on re-render, so the 60s tick is wasted if the component doesn't re-render for another reason.
warnings.suggestion: Remove the unused tick state entirely and use setInterval with direct DOM update, or use useEffect to track current time in state and derive remaining from it.

warnings.msg: Color variable is assigned via if/else ladder then conditionally overridden — colorClass can be set to one value in the if (line 58) and then replaced in the breached block (line 73). This works but is confusing.
warnings.suggestion: Simplify color logic: compute colorClass based on breached and ratio only, removing the separate reassignment in the return statement.

warnings.msg: Template literal `${colorClass} animate-pulse border-red-500` duplicates 'border-red-300' set inside colorClass for breached state — the border class is applied twice inconsistently.
warnings.suggestion: Remove the border-red-300 from colorClass and only use border-red-500 via the template literal when breached.

warnings.msg: setInterval has no cleanup guarantee if the component unmounts before the effect — useEffect cleanup is present but the interval closure captures stale tick reference if the component re-renders.
warnings.suggestion: Use a ref or state to track actual elapsed time rather than incrementing a counter.

warnings.msg: useCustomers is called with page=undefined and pageSize=20, but the query param construction (page=${undefined}) would produce invalid URL params since undefined coerces to the string 'undefined'.
warnings.suggestion: Use a default page value: useCustomers(page ?? 1, 20) or pass a definite page number from the parent.

warnings.msg: initialData is typed as Partial<TicketFormData> & { id?: number }, but fields like customer_id, channel, priority, sla_level are always strings in TicketFormData — no runtime validation ensures type correctness when editing pre-existing data.
warnings.suggestion: Add a type guard or parse initialData fields explicitly to assert their types before use.

warnings.msg: Number(data.customer_id) is called without checking whether customer_id is 0 — a value of 0 passes Number() without NaN, potentially sending { customer_id: 0 } to the API.
warnings.suggestion: Validate customer_id before Number(): if isNaN(Number(data.customer_id)) or data.customer_id === 0, show the form error instead of submitting.

warnings.msg: Customers data is cast with 'as Array<{ id: number; name: string }>' — any mismatch between the actual API response shape and this type assertion will cause silent runtime errors.
warnings.suggestion: Define a Customer type and use it for the response envelope instead of a generic cast.

warnings.msg: useEffect that resets form on initialData change has no cleanup (no return), and since it depends on reset, eslint-plugin-react-hooks would warn about missing reset from deps if not suppressed.
warnings.suggestion: Add reset to the dependency array: useEffect(() => { ... }, [initialData, reset]) — though this may cause infinite loops if reset is unstable.

warnings.msg: useReminders does not type its return value with ApiEnvelope — unlike every other query hook, it omits the generic and returns an untyped response, losing compile-time safety.
warnings.suggestion: Add <ApiEnvelope<Record<string, unknown>>> generic to the apiClient.get call in useReminders, consistent with all other hooks.

warnings.msg: useCustomers has a parameter named pageSize but is called from ticket-form-dialog.tsx with undefined as the first argument — the function defaults pageSize to 20 but page has no such default, so the first arg becomes page.
warnings.suggestion: Add a default: page = 1 to useCustomers signature so passing only pageSize works correctly.

warnings.msg: PaginatedResponse and ApiEnvelope are defined locally and not exported — other parts of the codebase like ticket-form-dialog cast to local anonymous types, preventing shared use.
warnings.suggestion: Export PaginatedResponse<T> and ApiEnvelope<T> so they can be reused across the app instead of duplicating inline Record<string, unknown> casts.

warnings.msg: useAddReply onSuccess invalidates both ticketReplies and ticketActivity query keys, but useUpdateTicket (line 209) only invalidates the generic ['tickets'] key rather than using qk.tickets() for consistency.
warnings.suggestion: Use qk.tickets() in useUpdateTicket onSuccess to keep query key construction centralized and consistent.

warnings.msg: psycopg2-binary and pymysql are listed as dependencies but the project uses asyncpg for async database access; they appear unused
warnings.suggestion: Remove psycopg2-binary and pymysql, or confirm they are consumed elsewhere in the codebase

warnings.msg: reportlab is listed as a dependency but is not used in the reviewed files
warnings.suggestion: Remove reportlab if it is not consumed by any reviewed file, or document where it is used

warnings.msg: mypy is listed in dev dependencies but CLAUDE.md notes that mypy is run via pre-push hook; ruff's select does not include type-checking rules (B, TRY)
warnings.suggestion: Ensure mypy is included in CI and that ruff ignores don't suppress type-checking gaps that mypy should catch

warnings.msg: HTTPException is imported but only used for the two manual validation handlers at lines 158 and 162; the project pattern routes AppException subclasses to a global handler, making manual HTTPException redundant
warnings.suggestion: Remove HTTPException import and raise a ValidationException instead, or drop the manual try/except blocks and rely on the global handler

warnings.msg: tenant_id=ctx.tenant_id or 0 uses a fallback of 0 for None, masking whether the real tenant is 0 or simply absent from the token
warnings.suggestion: Make tenant_id resolution explicit: raise HTTPException 401 if ctx.tenant_id is None, rather than silently coercing to 0

warnings.msg: assignee_id filter accepts 0 via ge=0 to represent 'unassigned', but TicketBulkUpdate also accepts ge=1 for its assigned_to, creating inconsistent semantics
warnings.suggestion: Standardise: use ge=0 consistently and treat 0 as 'no change / unassigned'; document the semantics

warnings.msg: Manual try/except ValueError handling for status and priority enums duplicates the Pydantic model validation already done via pattern in TicketCreate/TicketUpdate
warnings.suggestion: Remove the try/except blocks; if query params are invalid the enum constructor will raise ValueError caught by the global AppException handler

warnings.msg: bulk_update_tickets loops over ticket_ids sequentially without transaction safety; if one update fails mid-loop the already-updated tickets stay changed (partial failure)
warnings.suggestion: Wrap the loop in a transaction or clarify the docstring that the operation is best-effort and partial updates are intentional

warnings.msg: bulk_update_tickets docstring promises to skip tickets from other tenants, but the code does not check whether tickets were skipped — a silently ignored class of failures
warnings.suggestion: Collect and return the IDs of tickets that were skipped or not found, so callers can detect partial outcomes

warnings.msg: get_sla_breach_tickets constructs SLAService with ticket_service=TicketService(session), causing two service instances and two DB sessions for what is logically one operation
warnings.suggestion: Pass the already-instantiated TicketService from the router scope, or inject the session into SLAService and let it instantiate TicketService internally with the same session

warnings.msg: Rule 121 violation: ticket_service is a service instance passed as an optional constructor argument, not an AsyncSession; the convention requires the single constructor arg to be session
warnings.suggestion: Pass session: AsyncSession as the only constructor arg; instantiate TicketService(session) internally when needed, or accept it as an optional AsyncSession from the router

warnings.msg: remaining is a timedelta; the comparison remaining.total_seconds() < warning_threshold * 3600 is redundant since remaining is already derived from response_deadline - UTC.now()
warnings.suggestion: Simplify to remaining < timedelta(hours=warning_threshold) for clarity and correctness

warnings.msg: calculate_remaining_time is called at line 34 but returns a timedelta; however, calculate_remaining_time on line 57 can return a raw relativedelta if response_deadline is timezone-aware and datetime.now(UTC) is subtracted — check type consistency
warnings.suggestion: Ensure calculate_remaining_time always returns timedelta: cast result to timedelta() to guarantee type consistency across all code paths

warnings.msg: get_breach_tickets has an awkward optional tickets parameter that is also set internally from _ticket_service; the parameter name shadows the built-in
warnings.suggestion: Rename parameter from 'tickets' to 'ticket_list' or similar to avoid shadowing the built-in

warnings.msg: remaining is assigned from a conditional expression but can be either a timedelta or timedelta(0) — the guard at line 37 checks total_seconds() which is correct but the logic is duplicated in check_sla_breach
warnings.suggestion: Reuse check_sla_breach() as the single source of truth for breach detection rather than checking remaining.total_seconds() separately

warnings.msg: _AGENT_POOL = (1, 2, 3) is a module-level constant with magic numbers; agents must be real user IDs but there is no validation that these IDs exist
warnings.suggestion: Define _AGENT_POOL with a comment referencing the lookup source, and consider validating pool members against the users table on service init or first use

warnings.msg: add_reply has a TOCTOU race: two concurrent replies can both pass the not ticket.first_response_at check and each set first_response_at, leaving only the last writer's timestamp
warnings.suggestion: Use SELECT FOR UPDATE on the ticket row within the existing transaction to lock the ticket during first_response_at update, or rely on an atomic UPDATE with a WHERE clause that filters on first_response_at IS NULL

warnings.msg: get_ticket_activity uses content.like('%ticket#{ticket_id}%') — a leading-wildcard LIKE cannot use a B-tree index and will do a full table scan on the activity table
warnings.suggestion: Add a ticket_id column to the ActivityModel and index it, then replace the LIKE filter with a direct equality filter; alternatively add a GIN index on content if full-text search is needed

warnings.msg: add_reply returns TicketReplyModel but does not call session.flush() before the ticket update at line 249 — the reply has been added to the session but not yet flushed, making the relative ordering of reply insert and ticket update non-deterministic at the DB level
warnings.suggestion: Move session.add(reply) after the first_response_at update, or call await self.session.flush() before the UPDATE to ensure consistent ordering

warnings.msg: _to_str is a module-level helper that handles both enum and string inputs; it works but the pattern is duplicated across services — consider a shared utility in pkg.utils
warnings.suggestion: Extract _to_str to pkg.utils and import it, or rely on .value directly since the service only ever receives enum arguments from the router

warnings.msg: Test parameterized over async_session fixture but RBACService.has_permission is a @staticmethod requiring no DB; the fixture is unused and clutters test scope.
warnings.suggestion: Remove the async_session fixture parameter from all TestRBACServiceIntegration async tests — they test static in-memory logic that doesn't need DB access. Alternatively, test only the async DB-backed methods if they are added.

warnings.msg: Manually constructing a Ticket dataclass from models.ticket to simulate an expired ticket bypasses the ORM; the test exercises the SLA service but with a test double rather than a real persisted ticket.
warnings.suggestion: Consider inserting a real TicketModel row directly in the DB with a past response_deadline via raw SQL, so the test exercises the full stack including SLA query logic against a real ticket record.

warnings.msg: Same Ticket dataclass construction pattern as line 350 — test double instead of a real DB row.
warnings.suggestion: Insert a real ticket row into the DB with a past resolved_at to test the resolved-ticket path.

warnings.msg: Same Ticket dataclass construction pattern as line 350 — test double instead of a real DB row.
warnings.suggestion: Insert a real ticket row into the DB with resolved_at = now() to test the resolved branch.

warnings.msg: TriggerService.check_triggers uses page_size=10000 with no pagination boundary guard; a large campaign table could cause memory issues.
warnings.suggestion: Use a reasonable page_size (e.g. 1000) or paginate through results.

warnings.msg: TicketChannel, TicketPriority, TicketStatus imported from services.ticket_service rather than models.ticket where they are defined; violates project convention that enums live in models/ and services re-export them.
warnings.suggestion: Change to: from models.ticket import TicketChannel, TicketPriority, TicketStatus

warnings.msg: _seed_tenant returns a raw dict (result['id']), inconsistent with _seed_user/_seed_customer which return ORM object .id directly.
warnings.suggestion: Return result.id or result['id'] consistently across all seed helpers; prefer returning ORM objects for type safety.

warnings.msg: test_change_password calls change_password with no assertions on the result; the comment 'returns None on success' means the test passes vacuously without verifying the new password actually works.
warnings.suggestion: Add an assertion or call auth_svc.authenticate_user(old_password) to confirm the old password fails and/or a successful auth with the new password succeeds.

warnings.msg: _seed_customer uses hardcoded 'Test Customer' name and only f'test-{uuid}@example.com' for email variation; concurrent test runs with the same uuid segment could produce email uniqueness violations if the DB enforces unique email.
warnings.suggestion: Include the full uuid hex in the name as well: name=f'Test Customer {uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}' to avoid name uniqueness issues if that constraint is added later.

warnings.msg: test_assign_ticket expects ticket.assigned_to to be non-None after creation (auto-assigned), but if the agent pool (_AGENT_POOL = (1, 2, 3)) has no valid agents for this tenant, the assertion will fail in a real DB environment.
warnings.suggestion: Seed an agent user for the tenant before creating the ticket, or mock _next_agent in integration tests, so the assertion is deterministic rather than relying on hardcoded agent IDs.

warnings.msg: The auto-assign round-robin test does not verify round-robin ordering — only that both tickets get an integer; the test passes even if both receive the same agent.
warnings.suggestion: Assert ticket1.assigned_to != ticket2.assigned_to (or verify expected rotation pattern) to actually test round-robin behavior.

warnings.msg: Rule 124 violation: the mock_session fixture includes session.refresh = AsyncMock(); unit tests that call get_ticket_replies or get_ticket_activity (which call session.refresh internally) are testing with a no-op mock rather than verifying refresh behavior — could silently hide bugs where refresh fails.
warnings.suggestion: Ensure mock_session.refresh is configured to return/populate the actual mock object passed to it, or document that refresh is intentionally a no-op in this test file.

warnings.msg: Test name test_returns_replies_ordered_by_created_at_asc is 51 characters — exceeds the project's readable test-name guidance; consider renaming to test_replies_ordered_asc or test_replies_order_asc.
warnings.suggestion: Shorten test name to under 45 characters: test_replies_ordered_asc.

warnings.msg: test_breached_when_deadline_passed_and_not_resolved is a sync method but the class it lives in (TestSLABreachDetection) is not marked async — it runs fine but mixed async/sync test classes can cause pytest-asyncio discovery issues in some configurations.
warnings.suggestion: Mark the class as @pytest.mark.unit if not already configured, and consider grouping sync SLA tests in a separate class from async reply/activity tests.

warnings.msg: MagicMock instances lack type hints — reduces value of static analysis for test code.
warnings.suggestion: Annotate mock_service, mock_sla_service, mock_user_service with their actual types, e.g. `mock_service: MagicMock = MagicMock()` or use `create_autospec(TicketService)` for stricter mock shapes.

warnings.msg: Test name claims 'assignee_id_zero_rejected' but router schema enforces ge=1 (not ge=0), so this test exercises a code path that cannot exist in production.
warnings.suggestion: Change the test to assert on a different invalid value that is actually caught by the router, e.g. assignee_id=-1, or update the router schema to also reject 0 and write a test for that scenario.

warnings.msg: assign_ticket router calls UserService(session) to validate the assignee exists before assigning, but client_with_service only patches TicketService — the UserService call is not verified in any test.
warnings.suggestion: Add a test that verifies UserService.get_user_by_id is called (or that a NotFoundException from UserService propagates correctly) when assigning to a non-existent user.

warnings.msg: No test covers the assign_ticket endpoint with a non-existent assignee user — the UserService validation branch is exercised but not asserted.
warnings.suggestion: Add a test case: mock UserService.get_user_by_id to raise NotFoundException, call PUT /api/v1/tickets/1/assign with json={"assignee_id": 99}, and assert status 404.

warnings.msg: No tests exist for the POST /api/v1/tickets/bulk-update endpoint — the router has branching logic (assigned_to + status) that is entirely untested.
warnings.suggestion: Add TestBulkUpdateEndpoint with cases: success with status change, success with assignment, partial-not-found (one ticket missing, others updated).

warnings.msg: assert resp.status_code == 200 in test_success but does not verify the response body (assigned_to=5) is correctly serialized — only the mock was checked.
warnings.suggestion: Add assertion: assert resp.json()["data"]["assigned_to"] == 5 to verify the response envelope reflects the updated ticket.

warnings.msg: test_success for update_ticket asserts subject but not priority, channel, or assigned_to even though TicketUpdate schema accepts all three.
warnings.suggestion: Add assertions for all fields returned in the envelope, e.g. assert body["data"]["priority"] == "medium".

parsed.summary: Plan file describing the full ticket management UI implementation; no code issues present.

issues.message: useCustomers(1, 100) fetches a page of customers just to look up one name by ID; if the customer is beyond page 100 the name will be missing from the sidebar link.
issues.suggestion: Create a useCustomer(id) query (already exported in queries.ts) and fetch by ticket.customer_id directly: const { data: customerData } = useCustomer(Number(ticket.customer_id)); const customerName = customerData?.data?.name.

issues.message: initials() calls n[0] on every space-split token; if created_by is null/undefined/empty-string, n[0] is undefined and join produces 'UNDEFINEDUNDEFINED'.
issues.suggestion: Guard against empty parts: .map((n) => n && n[0] ? n[0] : '').join('')

issues.message: No loading skeleton shown while useTicketReplies or useTicketActivity are pending — the replies section and activity log will flash empty then populate, creating a jarring layout shift.
issues.suggestion: Add const { isLoading: repliesLoading } = useTicketReplies(ticketId); const { isLoading: activityLoading } = useTicketActivity(ticketId); and render skeletons or a spinner inside the Replies and Activity cards when those flags are true.

issues.message: onClick handler is attached to the <td> element itself; React treats synthetic events on <td> as non-interactive and the row-actions button may not receive stopPropagation reliably, risking the dropdown triggering unwanted navigation.
issues.suggestion: Move the onClick from <td className="... w-10" onClick={...}> to the <DropdownMenuTrigger> or wrap the <td> content in a div with pointer-events management.

issues.message: No error handling displayed for the useCustomers call; if the customers API fails the sidebar link silently falls back to '#{customer_id}' without user feedback.
issues.suggestion: Destructure isError from useCustomers and display a small inline warning or log the error.

issues.message: useEffect dependency array for the SLA toast check does not include toast; if the sonner toast function reference changes the effect won't re-run, though this is low-risk since sonner stable.
issues.suggestion: Add toast to the dependency array: useEffect(() => { ... }, [ticket, ticketId, toast]);

parsed.summary: Ticket detail page renders well but has no loading skeletons for replies/activity, fetches 100 customers just to find one name, and has a malformed initials() function.

issues.message: window.confirm() is a blocking browser dialog with a generic message; it bypasses the app's styling and accessibility conventions.
issues.suggestion: Replace with a confirm Dialog (Radix or shadcn Dialog) rendered inline with a destructive Cancel/Confirm pair.

issues.message: PRIORITY_COLORS includes both 'normal' and 'medium' keys but the plan spec and Select options only expose 'urgent/high/medium/low', so 'normal' is dead code; if the API ever returns 'normal' the color will differ from 'medium' despite being the same priority level.
issues.suggestion: Remove the 'normal' key from PRIORITY_COLORS: const PRIORITY_COLORS = { urgent: ..., high: ..., medium: ..., low: ... };

issues.message: useEffect dependency array is missing toast; if sonner's toast function reference changes the SLA breach toasts may use a stale closure.
issues.suggestion: Add toast to the dependency array: useEffect(() => { ... }, [isLoading, breachedTicketIds, toast]);

issues.message: Sort comparator uses av < bv ? -1 : av > bv ? 1 : 0 which coerces all values to booleans; for string values localeCompare would give more correct Unicode-aware ordering.
issues.suggestion: When sortKey is not 'response_deadline', use localeCompare: if (typeof av === 'string') return sortDir === 'asc' ? av.localeCompare(bv as string) : (bv as string).localeCompare(av);

parsed.summary: Tickets list page is well-structured with filtering, sorting, and Kanban toggle, but uses a blocking window.confirm for delete and has a dead 'normal' priority key in the color map.

issues.message: After a successful bulkUpdate mutation the component calls onClear() but does not reset bulkUpdate state; if the mutation is retried on a subsequent apply it may show isPending from the previous attempt.

issues.message: The assignee Select has no way to unassign tickets in bulk — the 'Assign to...' placeholder implies only 'select an agent to assign', leaving no UI affordance to clear an existing assignment.
issues.suggestion: Add a SelectItem value="" underneath the user options with label 'Unassign' or '—' so users can bulk-clear assignments.

issues.suggestion: Remove print statement; log only non-sensitive fields (e.g., user_id, tenant_id) if needed

issues.message: tenant_id=ctx.tenant_id or 0 uses a fallback of 0 for None, masking whether the real tenant is 0 or simply absent from the token
issues.suggestion: Make tenant_id resolution explicit: raise HTTPException 401 if ctx.tenant_id is None, rather than silently coercing to 0

issues.message: assignee_id filter accepts 0 via ge=0 to represent 'unassigned', but TicketBulkUpdate also accepts ge=1 for its assigned_to, creating inconsistent semantics
issues.suggestion: Standardise: use ge=0 consistently and treat 0 as 'no change / unassigned'; document the semantics

issues.message: Manual try/except ValueError handling for status and priority enums duplicates the Pydantic model validation already done via pattern in TicketCreate/TicketUpdate
issues.suggestion: Remove the try/except blocks; if query params are invalid the enum constructor will raise ValueError caught by the global AppException handler

issues.message: bulk_update_tickets loops over ticket_ids sequentially without transaction safety; if one update fails mid-loop the already-updated tickets stay changed (partial failure)
issues.suggestion: Wrap the loop in a transaction or clarify the docstring that the operation is best-effort and partial updates are intentional

issues.message: bulk_update_tickets docstring promises to skip tickets from other tenants, but the code does not check whether tickets were skipped — a silently ignored class of failures
issues.suggestion: Collect and return the IDs of tickets that were skipped or not found, so callers can detect partial outcomes

issues.message: get_sla_breach_tickets constructs SLAService with ticket_service=TicketService(session), causing two service instances and two DB sessions for what is logically one operation
issues.suggestion: Pass the already-instantiated TicketService from the router scope, or inject the session into SLAService and let it instantiate TicketService internally with the same session

parsed.summary: Multiple critical security issues (hardcoded JWT secret fallback, raw token/logging to stdout) and API design inconsistencies (tenant coercion, partial bulk-update failure, no skipped-ticket tracking) need resolution.

issues.message: Rule 121 violation: ticket_service is a service instance passed as an optional constructor argument, not an AsyncSession; the convention requires the single constructor arg to be session
issues.suggestion: Pass session: AsyncSession as the only constructor arg; instantiate TicketService(session) internally when needed, or accept it as an optional AsyncSession from the router

issues.message: remaining is a timedelta; the comparison remaining.total_seconds() < warning_threshold * 3600 is redundant since remaining is already derived from response_deadline - UTC.now()
issues.suggestion: Simplify to remaining < timedelta(hours=warning_threshold) for clarity and correctness

issues.message: calculate_remaining_time is called at line 34 but returns a timedelta; however, calculate_remaining_time on line 57 can return a raw relativedelta if response_deadline is timezone-aware and datetime.now(UTC) is subtracted — check type consistency
issues.suggestion: Ensure calculate_remaining_time always returns timedelta: cast result to timedelta() to guarantee type consistency across all code paths

issues.message: get_breach_tickets has an awkward optional tickets parameter that is also set internally from _ticket_service; the parameter name shadows the built-in
issues.suggestion: Rename parameter from 'tickets' to 'ticket_list' or similar to avoid shadowing the built-in

issues.message: remaining is assigned from a conditional expression but can be either a timedelta or timedelta(0) — the guard at line 37 checks total_seconds() which is correct but the logic is duplicated in check_sla_breach
issues.suggestion: Reuse check_sla_breach() as the single source of truth for breach detection rather than checking remaining.total_seconds() separately

parsed.summary: Constructor pattern violation (ticket_service should not be optional) and minor logic redundancy in remaining-time / breach detection are the main concerns.

issues.message: _AGENT_POOL = (1, 2, 3) is a module-level constant with magic numbers; agents must be real user IDs but there is no validation that these IDs exist
issues.suggestion: Define _AGENT_POOL with a comment referencing the lookup source, and consider validating pool members against the users table on service init or first use

issues.message: add_reply has a TOCTOU race: two concurrent replies can both pass the not ticket.first_response_at check and each set first_response_at, leaving only the last writer's timestamp
issues.suggestion: Use SELECT FOR UPDATE on the ticket row within the existing transaction to lock the ticket during first_response_at update, or rely on an atomic UPDATE with a WHERE clause that filters on first_response_at IS NULL

issues.message: get_ticket_activity uses content.like('%ticket#{ticket_id}%') — a leading-wildcard LIKE cannot use a B-tree index and will do a full table scan on the activity table
issues.suggestion: Add a ticket_id column to the ActivityModel and index it, then replace the LIKE filter with a direct equality filter; alternatively add a GIN index on content if full-text search is needed

issues.message: add_reply returns TicketReplyModel but does not call session.flush() before the ticket update at line 249 — the reply has been added to the session but not yet flushed, making the relative ordering of reply insert and ticket update non-deterministic at the DB level
issues.suggestion: Move session.add(reply) after the first_response_at update, or call await self.session.flush() before the UPDATE to ensure consistent ordering

issues.message: _to_str is a module-level helper that handles both enum and string inputs; it works but the pattern is duplicated across services — consider a shared utility in pkg.utils
issues.suggestion: Extract _to_str to pkg.utils and import it, or rely on .value directly since the service only ever receives enum arguments from the router

parsed.summary: Race condition in first_response_at, unindexed LIKE query for activity lookup, and magic agent IDs are the primary concerns; overall transaction management (flush-only, no commit) is correctly implemented.

issues.message: Test parameterized over async_session fixture but RBACService.has_permission is a @staticmethod requiring no DB; the fixture is unused and clutters test scope.
issues.suggestion: Remove the async_session fixture parameter from all TestRBACServiceIntegration async tests — they test static in-memory logic that doesn't need DB access. Alternatively, test only the async DB-backed methods if they are added.

issues.message: Manually constructing a Ticket dataclass from models.ticket to simulate an expired ticket bypasses the ORM; the test exercises the SLA service but with a test double rather than a real persisted ticket.
issues.suggestion: Consider inserting a real TicketModel row directly in the DB with a past response_deadline via raw SQL, so the test exercises the full stack including SLA query logic against a real ticket record.

issues.message: Same Ticket dataclass construction pattern as line 350 — test double instead of a real DB row.
issues.suggestion: Insert a real ticket row into the DB with a past resolved_at to test the resolved-ticket path.

issues.message: Same Ticket dataclass construction pattern as line 350 — test double instead of a real DB row.
issues.suggestion: Insert a real ticket row into the DB with resolved_at = now() to test the resolved branch.

issues.message: TriggerService.check_triggers uses page_size=10000 with no pagination boundary guard; a large campaign table could cause memory issues.
issues.suggestion: Use a reasonable page_size (e.g. 1000) or paginate through results.

parsed.summary: Tests for AutomationRules, DataIsolation, and RBAC are solid; SLA/Trigger tests that pass manually-constructed Ticket dataclasses instead of real DB rows should either use real ORM objects or be moved to unit tests.

issues.message: _seed_user helper defaults to tenant_id=1, but callers in TestTicketServiceIntegration and TestSLAServiceIntegration omit the tenant_id argument; tickets and users end up in different tenants causing cross-tenant data leaks or NotFoundException failures.
issues.suggestion: Change the default to require_explicit: def _seed_user(async_session, tenant_id: int, **overrides) and update all callers to pass tenant_id explicitly, e.g. _seed_user(async_session, tenant_id) everywhere.

issues.message: _seed_customer helper also defaults to tenant_id=1; same cross-tenant data issue as _seed_user above.
issues.suggestion: Change the default to require_explicit: def _seed_customer(async_session, tenant_id: int, **overrides) and update all callers to pass tenant_id explicitly.

issues.message: TicketChannel, TicketPriority, TicketStatus imported from services.ticket_service rather than models.ticket where they are defined; violates project convention that enums live in models/ and services re-export them.
issues.suggestion: Change to: from models.ticket import TicketChannel, TicketPriority, TicketStatus

issues.message: _seed_tenant returns a raw dict (result['id']), inconsistent with _seed_user/_seed_customer which return ORM object .id directly.
issues.suggestion: Return result.id or result['id'] consistently across all seed helpers; prefer returning ORM objects for type safety.

issues.message: test_change_password calls change_password with no assertions on the result; the comment 'returns None on success' means the test passes vacuously without verifying the new password actually works.
issues.suggestion: Add an assertion or call auth_svc.authenticate_user(old_password) to confirm the old password fails and/or a successful auth with the new password succeeds.

parsed.summary: Two critical tenant_id default bugs cause cross-tenant data mixing in TicketService and SLAService tests; the file-level seed helpers must require explicit tenant_id on all callers.

issues.message: _seed_customer uses hardcoded 'Test Customer' name and only f'test-{uuid}@example.com' for email variation; concurrent test runs with the same uuid segment could produce email uniqueness violations if the DB enforces unique email.
issues.suggestion: Include the full uuid hex in the name as well: name=f'Test Customer {uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}' to avoid name uniqueness issues if that constraint is added later.

issues.message: test_assign_ticket expects ticket.assigned_to to be non-None after creation (auto-assigned), but if the agent pool (_AGENT_POOL = (1, 2, 3)) has no valid agents for this tenant, the assertion will fail in a real DB environment.
issues.suggestion: Seed an agent user for the tenant before creating the ticket, or mock _next_agent in integration tests, so the assertion is deterministic rather than relying on hardcoded agent IDs.

issues.message: The auto-assign round-robin test does not verify round-robin ordering — only that both tickets get an integer; the test passes even if both receive the same agent.
issues.suggestion: Assert ticket1.assigned_to != ticket2.assigned_to (or verify expected rotation pattern) to actually test round-robin behavior.

parsed.summary: Seed helpers and auto-assign test logic are mostly sound; one hardcoded agent pool dependency creates fragility for real-DB runs.

issues.message: Rule 124 violation: the mock_session fixture includes session.refresh = AsyncMock(); unit tests that call get_ticket_replies or get_ticket_activity (which call session.refresh internally) are testing with a no-op mock rather than verifying refresh behavior — could silently hide bugs where refresh fails.
issues.suggestion: Ensure mock_session.refresh is configured to return/populate the actual mock object passed to it, or document that refresh is intentionally a no-op in this test file.

issues.message: Test name test_returns_replies_ordered_by_created_at_asc is 51 characters — exceeds the project's readable test-name guidance; consider renaming to test_replies_ordered_asc or test_replies_order_asc.
issues.suggestion: Shorten test name to under 45 characters: test_replies_ordered_asc.

issues.message: test_breached_when_deadline_passed_and_not_resolved is a sync method but the class it lives in (TestSLABreachDetection) is not marked async — it runs fine but mixed async/sync test classes can cause pytest-asyncio discovery issues in some configurations.
issues.suggestion: Mark the class as @pytest.mark.unit if not already configured, and consider grouping sync SLA tests in a separate class from async reply/activity tests.

parsed.summary: Unit test structure is clean and well-organized; main concern is the session.refresh mock behavior and naming length in one test.

issues.message: MagicMock instances lack type hints — reduces value of static analysis for test code.
issues.suggestion: Annotate mock_service, mock_sla_service, mock_user_service with their actual types, e.g. `mock_service: MagicMock = MagicMock()` or use `create_autospec(TicketService)` for stricter mock shapes.

issues.message: Test name claims 'assignee_id_zero_rejected' but router schema enforces ge=1 (not ge=0), so this test exercises a code path that cannot exist in production.
issues.suggestion: Change the test to assert on a different invalid value that is actually caught by the router, e.g. assignee_id=-1, or update the router schema to also reject 0 and write a test for that scenario.

issues.message: assign_ticket router calls UserService(session) to validate the assignee exists before assigning, but client_with_service only patches TicketService — the UserService call is not verified in any test.
issues.suggestion: Add a test that verifies UserService.get_user_by_id is called (or that a NotFoundException from UserService propagates correctly) when assigning to a non-existent user.

issues.message: No test covers the assign_ticket endpoint with a non-existent assignee user — the UserService validation branch is exercised but not asserted.
issues.suggestion: Add a test case: mock UserService.get_user_by_id to raise NotFoundException, call PUT /api/v1/tickets/1/assign with json={"assignee_id": 99}, and assert status 404.

issues.message: No tests exist for the POST /api/v1/tickets/bulk-update endpoint — the router has branching logic (assigned_to + status) that is entirely untested.
issues.suggestion: Add TestBulkUpdateEndpoint with cases: success with status change, success with assignment, partial-not-found (one ticket missing, others updated).

issues.message: assert resp.status_code == 200 in test_success but does not verify the response body (assigned_to=5) is correctly serialized — only the mock was checked.
issues.suggestion: Add assertion: assert resp.json()["data"]["assigned_to"] == 5 to verify the response envelope reflects the updated ticket.

issues.message: test_success for update_ticket asserts subject but not priority, channel, or assigned_to even though TicketUpdate schema accepts all three.
issues.suggestion: Add assertions for all fields returned in the envelope, e.g. assert body["data"]["priority"] == "medium".

parsed.summary: Well-structured router unit test with clear class organization and descriptive names; gaps include untested bulk-update endpoint, under-verified assign and update assertions, and one test whose precondition cannot occur in production.
